title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π = π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. It is free profinite on loops ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞ with ℓ_0ℓ_1ℓ_∞ = 1. ρ is the order-3 automorphism ℓ_0 → ℓ_1 → ℓ_∞ → ℓ_0, written i ↦ i+1 with 0+1=1, 1+1=∞, ∞+1=0. L_i denotes the procyclic subgroup generated by ℓ_i, which is also its centralizer.

What \tilde M_{0,3} is. It is a group of (outer-type) automorphisms u of Π. Each u maps every ℓ_i to a conjugate of ℓ_i^λ with λ = χ(u) ∈ Ẑ^*, and u commutes with ρ up to an inner automorphism.

The group S\tilde M_{0,3} (previous page). It consists of quadruples (u, g_0, g_1, g_∞) with u(ℓ_i) = int(g_i^{-1})(ℓ_i^λ). The product is a semidirect-type law (5).

The kernel (this page). Forgetting the g_i gives a surjection S\tilde M_{0,3} → \tilde M_{0,3}. Its kernel is {(1, f_0, f_1, f_∞) : f_i ∈ L_i}, because each g_i is determined up to the centralizer of ℓ_i. This gives (7): 1 → Ẑ^3 → S\tilde M_{0,3} → \tilde M_{0,3} → 1. In words, the indeterminacy of a 'tangential base point' at each of the three cusps.

The refined subgroup S_0 (8). Grothendieck now uses the ρ-compatibility of u, written (9): uρu^{-1} = int(g)∘ρ, i.e. g = [u,ρ] ∈ Π. Given f_i satisfying (10), he propagates it by (11): f_{i+1}^{-1} = g·ρ(f_i^{-1}). Iterating gives f_{i+2}^{-1} = g ρ(g) ρ^2(f_i^{-1}).

Why the propagation closes up. Going round the full 3-cycle returns f_i^{-1}, because g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1 and ρ^3 = id. The first identity follows from ρ^3 = 1: we have (int(g)ρ)^3 = int(g ρ(g) ρ^2(g)) ρ^3 = uρ^3u^{-1} = id. Since Π has trivial center, the inner automorphism int(g ρ(g) ρ^2(g)) being trivial forces g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1.

Why the propagated f's are valid. With uρ = int(g)ρu one gets u(ℓ_{i+1}) = int(g)ρ(int(f_i^{-1})ℓ_i^λ) = int(g ρ(f_i^{-1}))(ℓ_{i+1}^λ). So the propagated f_{i+1} is again a valid choice.

What this produces (next page). The subgroup S_0 \tilde M^!_{0,3} ≅ {(u, f_0)} is an extension by Ẑ, from which (via the diagonal Ẑ → Ẑ^3) the extension by Ẑ^3 is pushed out. Put differently, the ρ-symmetry reduces the three independent cusp ambiguities to a single diagonal one.

Purpose. The goal is a canonical group law and a lifting of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group into automorphism data that includes conjugators (the 'f' of GT). It is a precursor to the GT relation in the 3-cycle form f(z,x)z^m f(y,z)y^m f(x,y)x^m = 1.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. The closing identity g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1 is asserted without proof. It holds because (int(g)ρ)^3 = uρ^3u^{-1} = id and Π̂_{0,3} has trivial center; the note leaves this implicit.
The construction needs ρ(ℓ_i) = ℓ_{i+1} exactly, not merely up to conjugacy. This holds for the standard presentation ℓ_0ℓ_1ℓ_∞ = 1 with ρ the cyclic shift, but is not stated.

Notation drifts between \tilde M_{0,3} and \tilde M^!_{0,3} (the λ = 1 or 'special' variant). The parenthetical in (10) refers to S\tilde M^!_{0,3}, while (8) is written as a subgroup of \tilde M_{0,3}. Per the next page, (8) should read S_0\tilde M_{0,3} ⊂ S\tilde M_{0,3}, i.e. a subgroup of the S-extension.

ideas.what: Extension of the (outer) automorphism group of π̂_{0,3} preserving the inertia classes by Ẑ^3, recording a chosen conjugator g_i for each cusp (the ambiguity of tangential base points)
ideas.modern_name: Lifting of GT / Aut^*(F̂_2) to automorphisms with chosen cusp conjugators; braid-type extension of GT by inertia
ideas.where_published: Only the general program in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); not this explicit construction

ideas.what: Using the order-3 symmetry ρ with u ρ u^{-1} = g ρ to propagate a conjugator f_0 to f_1 and f_∞, with consistency from g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1, yielding a sub-extension by diagonal Ẑ
ideas.modern_name: The 3-cycle (hexagon-type) relation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group; normalization of f via ρ-symmetry

missed.claim: An explicit, pre-Drinfeld-style formulation of the GT 3-cycle relation as a cocycle condition g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1 for g = [u,ρ]. It is used to cut the Ẑ^3 ambiguity of cusp conjugators down to a diagonal Ẑ, giving an intermediate extension S_0\tilde M_{0,3}. This is equivalent in content to known GT normalizations, but the presentation as a 'finer' extension by Ẑ (pushed out along the diagonal) is a viewpoint not standard in the literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents that Grothendieck derived the cyclic (hexagon-type) relation from the ρ-commutation in his 'longue marche' notes, independently of Drinfeld. It also shows the extension structure of GT-type groups by inertia.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, correct derivation of what amounts to the GT 3-cycle relation and an extension by diagonal Ẑ. The mathematics is known since Drinfeld/Ihara, but this explicit unpublished Grothendieck formulation is of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: The header '{+éq.[?]+}' is actually the page number '491' (the next page is 492).
'de commuter rationnellement[?] à ρ' is uncertain; the sense is 'commute up to inner automorphism with ρ' (perhaps 'relativement' or 'extérieurement').
In (8) the intended statement (per the next page) is S_0\tilde M_{0,3} ⊂ S\tilde M_{0,3}, not ⊂ \tilde M_{0,3}.
In (10) the left side is u(ℓ_i), with ℓ_i the loops (written l_i in the transcription).
